clue.text: Dickens opens with Barnaby, a menial

indicators.note: what opens the word Dickens is its first letter, so only that initial is taken

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel, so his surname is supplied

explanation.surface: A Dickens novel begins with Barnaby, a lowly servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' takes only the first letter of Dickens, D; Barnaby's surname in the Dickens novel is RUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge is a person who does dull, servile work, which is what a menial is.

clue.text: Notes on intended challenge

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first, so the notes precede the intended

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
one's intended is one's fiancé, the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: Some musical notes written on an engagement challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is a bold refusal to obey, a challenge to authority.

clue.text: Words of encouragement from one raising issue?

definitions.text: Words of encouragement from one raising issue?

parts.words: Words of encouragement from one raising issue?
parts.note: issue means offspring, so the clue pictures a parent lifting a small child and saying the cheerful phrase people use when picking up a toddler

explanation.surface: A complainant raising an issue offers a few encouraging words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising issue' looks like bringing up a matter for discussion; issue is children, and raising is lifting one up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said cheerily when lifting a child or helping someone who has stumbled.

clue.text: Depression in inglenook

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of inglenook, so in signals a hidden run

explanation.surface: Feeling low while sitting in a fireside nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, a depression in the land.

clue.text: Around Douglas, can they not show displeasure?

definitions.text: Around Douglas, can they not show displeasure?

parts.words: Around Douglas, can they not show displeasure?
parts.note: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, and the tailless cats bred there cannot swish a tail to show annoyance

explanation.surface: A question whether people around a man called Douglas are unable to show they are annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like a man's name but is the capital of the Isle of Man, a British island in the Irish Sea whose native cat breed has no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's breed of tailless cat is named after the island's people and adjective.

clue.text: Dead men astonishingly made better

indicators.note: astonishingly suggests the letters of dead men are thrown into a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Corpses miraculously restored to health.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amended has been corrected or improved.

clue.text: Foreigners hating our broken phoneboxes?

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of phoneboxes are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: People who blame outsiders for vandalised telephone kiosks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: people hating foreigners might blame them for broken phoneboxes, and 'broken' rearranges PHONEBOXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophobes are people with a fear or hatred of foreigners, the kind who blame them for vandalism.

clue.text: On board, one could delay men getting home

definitions.text: On board, one could delay men getting home

parts.words: On board, one could delay men getting home
parts.note: on the board of the children's game with serpents and climbing rungs, landing on a serpent slides the players' counters back and delays their reaching the last square

explanation.surface: Someone aboard a ship who might keep the crew from returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is a games board, and 'men' are the counters on a board game of serpents and climbing rungs.
explanation.definitionFit: An adder is a snake, and snakes on the game board send counters backwards.

clue.text: Bow address?

definitions.meaning: a bow is a gesture of respect or greeting
to address someone can mean to greet them formally

explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture of greeting or respect, as a bow is, and to greet someone is to address them.

clue.text: Jumbo pilot with a mouth disorder

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of a mouth are put out of their order

explanation.surface: An elephant-driver with an ailment of the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo is a famous elephant's name, used for any elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is the person who drives and guides an elephant.

clue.text: Looking after others' children from New Forest, takes time

indicators.note: New tells us the letters of forest are made into something new

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Childcare from the New Forest, a national park in southern England, takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Forest' is a real place name; here 'New' only rearranges FOREST to FOSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fosterage is the bringing up of a child who is not one's own.

clue.text: An old-fashioned lumpy solution here

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters of an old are formed afresh

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned remedy that is lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one word; it splits into 'old', the fodder with 'An', and 'fashioned', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodal relates to nodes, which are knots or swellings, so it describes something knobbly.

clue.text: Second note of Verdi opera

parts.note: to second someone is to support or aid them
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: The second musical note of a Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number; it is a verb meaning to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Dryad's methanol

definitions.meaning: a dryad is a nymph of the trees in Greek myth
methanol is an alcohol once distilled from timber

explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph, a spirit of the forest, and methanol was traditionally made by distilling timber.

clue.text: Flatfish Authority providing fun for kids

parts.note: a skate is a kind of flatfish
a board is a governing body or authority

explanation.surface: A fish-industry authority laying on entertainment for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A skateboard is a wheeled plank children ride for fun.

clue.text: Novel game at home, using the wings

definitions.text: Novel game at home, using the wings

parts.words: Novel game at home, using the wings
parts.note: Dickens wrote a story about the chirping insect on the hearth, and the bat-and-ball game uses fielders on the wings; the insect chirps with its wings

explanation.surface: A new game played indoors using the flanks of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new'; it points to Dickens's The Cricket on the Hearth, 'at home'. The chirping insect sings by rubbing its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the bat-and-ball game and the chirping insect of Dickens's Christmas book.

clue.text: Retirement party in beloved, fragrant wood

indicators.note: in places the turned party within the word for beloved

parts.note: dear means beloved

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A retirement party held in a dear, sweet-smelling wooden hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' turns DO into OD, which goes inside DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The deodar is a Himalayan cedar valued for its scented timber.

clue.text: Opposed to insincere church responses?

definitions.note: a plural phrase for the alternate singing, which the answer names as a practice

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to
phony means fake or insincere

explanation.surface: Objecting to hollow responses in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is alternate singing by two choirs, call and response in worship.

clue.text: Stick to keep the ball rolling

definitions.meaning: to stick at something is to persist
an idiom for carrying on with an activity

explanation.definitionFit: To continue is to persist or carry on, the sense of sticking at something and keeping the ball rolling.

clue.text: Termly managment of evergreen shrub

indicators.note: management means handling or arranging, so the letters of termly are rearranged

explanation.surface: The school-term care of a garden shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managment' is printed so, a slip for management, which arranges TERMLY afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Made of clay from Teheran

indicators.note: made from tells us the answer is built out of the letters that follow
with made, this says the answer is constructed out of the letters of the city name

explanation.surface: A pot made of clay that comes from Iran's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made ... from' rearranges TEHERAN, an older spelling of Tehran.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes pots and vessels of baked earth such as terracotta.

clue.text: Master of some art, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that some art may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at a few of the arts, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master, especially a distinguished musician or conductor.

clue.text: Small car no good for bringing up ores

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: A small car is useless for hauling up rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Mining is the extraction of minerals from the ground.

clue.text: Unkempt fellow has some neck!

definitions.meaning: the back of the neck, by which a cat is lifted

explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is an untidy person, and the scruff is the nape by which an animal is held.

clue.text: Wild climbing peach, yellowish-brown on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside places the colour within the peach

parts.note: a cling is a clingstone peach
amber is a yellowish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A wild climbing peach tree whose fruit is amber within.
explanation.definitionFit: Clambering is climbing awkwardly using hands and feet, a scrambling ascent.

clue.text: Stroll in Lakeland town with no pretentiousness

indicators.note: with no means the word for pretentiousness is taken away

parts.note: Ambleside is a town in the Lake District of northern England
side is airs or pretentiousness

explanation.surface: A walk around a Lake District town without any airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambleside is a town in the Lake District, England's mountainous Lakeland. SIDE, British slang for putting on airs, is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Hot water stain

definitions.meaning: to be in hot water is to be in trouble

explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a difficult situation, as in being in a spot, and a small mark or blemish.

clue.text: Quarters in ancient city for employer

indicators.note: in puts the two quarters inside the ancient city's name

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
S for south is one compass quarter
E for east is another compass quarter

explanation.surface: Lodgings in an old city for one's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like lodgings; it gives two compass points, S and E, put inside UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs something, making use of it.

clue.text: Complete shadow in Burma jungle?

indicators.note: a jungle is a tangle, so the letters of the country are tangled up

explanation.surface: Deep shade under the Burmese jungle canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed text lost 'Bur'; the clue reads 'Burma jungle', and 'jungle' tangles BURMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the fully dark central part of a shadow, as in an eclipse.

clue.text: Bequeaths with no effort at all

definitions.meaning: easily, as a winner who never had to try

explanation.definitionFit: To hand down is to pass on to the next generation, and to win by that phrase is to win easily.

clue.text: Was he never an "in' writer?

parts.note: in cricket the side not batting is out in the field rather than in, so the novelist's surname describes a team never in

explanation.surface: A question whether an author was ever fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like fashionable; in cricket the batting side is 'in' and the other side is fielding. Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding was the eighteenth-century English novelist, and fielding is what the non-batting team does.

clue.text: Diamond pattern knitted early around head of glen

indicators.note: around wraps the rearranged letters about the head of glen
knitted means worked together, so the letters of early are rearranged
head of takes the first letter of glen

explanation.surface: A diamond pattern knitted early near the top of a Scottish valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' rearranges EARLY to ARYLE, which goes 'around' G, the head of glen.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is a knitting design of diamonds in several colours, found on socks and sweaters.
